question: Where can I get a list of stand-alone battery storage (BESS) projects currently in permitting in the United Kingdom, with location, power (MW), developer, permitting stage and date?

answer.summary: The UK REPD publishes a quarterly list with battery and stand-alone storage filters, planning milestones and project details for all four nations. It is a snapshot above 150 kW, not a complete live register. Check each application with its planning authority; the Northern Ireland portal excludes some records online.
main_caveats: REPD can lag: Belfast LA04/2020/1724/F is listed as submitted despite a 2023 council report marking it invalid.
The ECU screening outcome is not planning consent; the Netherton application dates require reconciliation.
The Northern Ireland register is not fully online, and Mid Ulster has a separate portal.
Connection and planning permission are separate milestones.
In October 2026, 32 of 271 rows tagged stand-alone and Application Submitted lacked MW. This is a snapshot count, and the stand-alone classification needs checking.
answer.confidence_reason: The extract was downloaded and Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish case documents checked; completeness and several sources remain unverified.

steps: Download the CSV and parse using Windows-1252: UTF-8 decoding failed in this test.
Start with Technology Type = Battery and Storage Type = Stand-alone Storage. Check the case for co-located generation.

For pending cases start with Planning Application Submitted and review Appeal Lodged separately. For the wider pre-operation scope retain Planning Permission Granted, Appeal Granted and Under Construction as separate stages. Trim and match labels case-insensitively; verify Revised cases against their current references.
Use the date column for the chosen milestone (submission, grant, appeal or start of construction). Verify current status with the competent authority using the planning reference.
reading_traps: The file is a quarterly snapshot, not a real-time register or proof of completeness.
Permission, start of construction and connection are different milestones.
Netherton screening opinion dated 9 May 2025 was Non-EIA, not permission; application letter is dated 18 September 2025 while REPD gives 21 August 2025. Verify the date with the authority.
Northern Ireland coordinates need a separate grid check; the Netherton sample alone does not validate all coordinates.
Of the 271 stand-alone records with Planning Application Submitted, 32 have no Installed Capacity (MWelec).

The Storage Type filter is the publisher’s classification, not proof that the site has no other technology: REPD 15823 names wind turbines and battery but is classified Stand-alone Storage. Check application documents.
Belfast LA04/2020/1724/F remains Application Submitted in the extract, but a 2023 council report calls it Application Invalid; a later application has a separate reference.
For Abergelli the council weekly list gives map reference 265242 201648, while the REPD row has 265117 201649; do not treat these as surveyed boundaries.
Four sample coordinates transform plausibly to the named areas using EPSG:27700, including Belfast, but no full-coordinate audit was carried out.
